state.description: Tropical Depression 29W is located 555 miles northeast of Chuuk, moving northwest at 13 mph. A turn more to the west is expected to occur over the next 24 hours. As 29W continues it's journey to the Marianas, rapid intensification is possible. This would result in increased west to southwest monsoon flow will increase. This will allow for showers to increase in coverage any intensity, with locally heavy rainfall likely. At this time, 2 to 4 inches of rainfall may develop, with locally higher amounts possible. If 29W can intensify a little faster than anticipated, or if it takes a due west track, this could open door for isolated wind gusts to 30 to 35 knots to develop. Seas currently look to increase 1 to 3 feet, topping out near 7 feet, but again, this could be higher if 29W tracks closer to Chuuk or strengthens faster. Folks with intra-island travel should delay any travel for a few days until the developing tropical depression has passed.

AQATWC The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued a PM-10 High Pollution [alert] for Douglas on Friday. An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-10 concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects increase as air quality deteriorates. Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air contaminant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions, especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A decrease in physical activity is recommended. Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid using gas-powered lawn equipment. For details on this High Pollution [alert], visit the ADEQ internet site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/douglas or call 602-771-2300.

state.description: A stronger atmospheric river is expected to move over the panhandle beginning early Thursday morning and continuing through at least Friday morning. This includes the cities of Ketchikan And Metlakatla. * WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations. Street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Rain totals between early Thursday morning and late Friday morning for the Ketchikan and Metlakatla area are currently expected around 4 to 6 inches, with higher rain totals favoring southern facing mountainsides. The chances of this to occur are around 30% at this time.

A series of fronts is bringing multiple rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle as of early Friday morning. This second round of heavy rain has brought around 2 to 3 inches of rainfall to the area over the last 24 hours, with ongoing moderate rainfall rates of around 0.1 to 0.2 inches reported within the last hour. An additional 0.5 to 1 inch of rain is expected into late Friday morning as this system pushes out of the area. Highest rain amounts are expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands, with locally lower or higher amounts possible due to terrain effects. Heaviest rainfall rates will come to an end through Friday morning with intermittent rain showers continuing through Friday afternoon across the area. While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding anticipated at this time. Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the situation and update our forecast.

state.description: A strong storm system is expected to move into the northern half of the Alaska Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast Monday night and continuing through Tuesday. Beginning Monday night for Yakutat and spreading eastward into early Tuesday morning, periods of heavy rain will begin and continue through the day on Tuesday. For Yakutat, Sitka, Pelican, and Elfin Cove, rain totals over a period of 36 hours is around 3 to 6 inches, with higher amounts near Yakutat and lower amounts near Sitka. For the Icy Strait corridor, including Hoonah and northern Admiralty Island, rain totals over the same time frame are around 2-3 inches, similar to the previous storm. For context, these totals are uncommon for this time of year, but are not historically extreme.

state.description: * WHAT....Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or more are expected. * WHERE...Guam Coastal Waters and Rota Coastal Waters. * WHEN...Onset of damaging winds beginning Saturday night. Onset of destructive winds Sunday morning. Damaging winds will continue into at least Sunday night, possibly longer if conditions warrant. * IMPACTS...Destructive winds will produce dangerous seas that could damage, capsize or sink vessels, along with drastically reducing visibilities in heavy rain. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tropical Storm Champi (29W) continues to move quickly toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains subject to change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal waters, with damaging winds moving in Saturday night and lasting into at least Sunday night. Champi is expected to strengthen further today and Saturday as it approaches, then move through the region as a typhoon Sunday morning. Seas will quickly rise, with significant sea heights reaching as high as 35 feet during closest passage of Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may continue into Monday.
state.instruction: Prepare for the passage of a typhoon Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions are expected to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely dangerous for any vessels of larger size. As Tropical Storm Champi approaches, stay in safe harbor.

state.description: ...RED FLAG [alert] IN EFFECT FROM 10 PM THIS EVENING TO 11 AM PDT FRIDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTH BAY INTERIOR MOUNTAINS... .Moderate offshore winds will develop Thursday evening into Friday morning over the North Bay Interior Mountains. Conditions will be very dry with very poor overnight humidity recoveries only reaching 14 to 24 percent. Rapid fire spread is possible given the combination of gusty northerly winds and very dry overnight conditions. The National Weather Service in San Francisco CA has issued a Red Flag [alert] in effect from 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT Friday. * AFFECTED AREA...North Bay Interior Mountains. * TIMING...From 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT Friday. * WINDS 20 FOOT...North winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 40 mph. The highest peaks above 4000ft will see gusts up to 60 mph. * RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 16 to 20 percent. * IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
state.instruction: A Red Flag [alert] is issued when weather conditions that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening are forecast. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to receive information from authorities. Please advise responding agencies or fire crews in the field of this fire weather alert. Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire. Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks. Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember, one less spark, one less flame. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan! Where will you go? How will you get there? Do you have your go kit ready to go? Who will you call to let others know you are safe? Visit ready.gov/plan for more information.

state.instruction: If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of distance ahead of you.

state.description: * WHAT...For the Small Craft [alert], northeast winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and seas 7 to 10 ft. For the Gale [alert], north winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and seas 9 to 14 ft expected. * WHERE...Coastal waters from Fenwick Island DE to Chincoteague VA out 20 NM. * WHEN...For the Small Craft [alert], until 4 AM EDT Monday. For the Gale [alert], from 4 AM Monday to 7 AM EDT Wednesday. * IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Gale conditions could persist into mid to late week.
state.instruction: Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions. Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the vessel for hazardous conditions.
